title: Chola Dynasty
summary: Tamil dynasty of south India which, from around the middle of the 9th century, held Tanjavur (Thanjavur), its capital for the rest of its dominance; the empire was effectively founded under Aditya Chola (r. 871–907). Between 985 and 1024 it reached Sri Lanka, Bengal and parts of Sumatra and Malaya; the dynasty ended in 1279.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia says the Cholas began to assert authority around the middle of the 9th century and names Aditya Chola (r. 871-907) as effective founder.

as_recorded.value: Around the middle of the 9th century
The dynasty declined and ended in 1279

where.modern_name: Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India (capital pinned: Tanjavur/Thanjavur, per WHE the capital for the duration of Chola dominance; Rajendra I later built a new capital for a brief period)
where.historical_name: Tanjavur (Thanjavur), capital of the Chola Empire

importance.justification: The dynasty whose temples, listed by UNESCO as Great Living Chola Temples, testify to Chola achievements in architecture, sculpture, painting and bronze casting.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List, full dataset (XML) with site coordinates

reviewer_note: Start date is approximate (mid-9th century per WHE; other pages seen only in search results give c. 848 or c. 850). The 985-1024 expansion claim is from the short Encyclopedia.com entry. Capital: Tanjavur for most of the period; WHE also says Rajendra I built a new capital further north for a brief period.
